title: Platform systems & services: ops playbook, runbooks, dashboards, roadmap, team wiki (Q2 2026)
author: Elena Park
body:
Overview

This page is the canonical platform systems & services operational playbook for Q2 2026. It consolidates the inventory of critical platform services, ownership, how-to operational procedures (deploys, dashboard creation, alert tuning), runbooks for high-severity incidents, a short retrospective on recent incidents, and the team-level roadmap and wiki pointers. Use this page as the primary reference during on-call and planning.

Goals
- Reduce mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for P0/P1 incidents to under 30 minutes.
- Keep inference-hosting SLOs met: 99th percentile API latency < 200ms for small models, < 500ms for large models; error rate < 0.1%.
- Improve alert precision to reduce noise by 30% vs. Q1 2026.

Systems & services inventory (critical)
- platform-control-plane: service that coordinates deployments, feature flags, and rollout policies. Owner: Platform Core.
- metrics-ingest: Prometheus pushgateway + relabel adapters used for ingesting service metrics. Owner: Observability.
- gpu-orchestrator: Kubernetes-backed controller scheduling GPU pools for Dedicated and Private. Owner: Serving Runtime.
- traffic-router: Envoy-based global router with smart-routing policies. Owner: Edge & Routing.
- kv-cache: Redis ring used for prefix/KV caching for inference sessions. Owner: Caching Team.
- telemetry-processor: Batch pipeline that aggregates evaluation and quality signals. Owner: Applied ML & Evals.

Ownership & escalation
- Primary oncall: platform-oncall@redwood.com (rotation in PagerDuty: Platform-Core SRE schedule).
- Secondary: infra-sre@redwood.com.
- PagerDuty playbook references: PD escalation policies "Platform P0", "Platform P1".
- Slack channels: #platform-oncall (alerts & postmortems), #platform-ops (ops discussion).

How-tos: Deploying a service (standard flow)
1. Open the service repo and confirm CI green (GitHub Actions).
2. Bump chart version in charts/<service>/Chart.yaml and update image tag.
3. Create PR with Helm values change and link associated Jira ticket. Include rollout strategy and canary percentage.
4. Merge requires 2 approvals from service owners and passing integration tests.
5. Trigger deploy: `./scripts/deploy.sh --env production --service <service> --chart-version <version>`.
6. Monitor rollout in the Deployments dashboard (Grafana) and check Service SLO panel.
7. If canary fails, rollback: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/<service> -n <ns>`.

Creating/Updating a Grafana dashboard (quick guide)
- Dashboard naming convention: "PLATFORM / <team> / <service> / <metric-set>".
- Panels should include: p50/p90/p99 latency, request rate, error rate, CPU/GPU usage, queue depth, and cache hit ratio.
- Add drilldowns to relevant logs (Loki) and traces (Tempo).
- Save a JSON model to the dashboard repo: `infra/grafana/dashboards/<team>/<dashboard-name>.json` and open PR.
- Owners must add `grafana-owner: <github-handle>` in dashboard metadata.

Alerts & thresholds (current recommended rules)
- Alert: PLATFORM_API_HIGH_5XX_RATE
  - Condition: 5xx error rate > 0.2% for 5m
  - Severity: P1
  - Notify: #platform-oncall, page primary
- Alert: PLATFORM_INFERENCE_LATENCY_P99
  - Condition: p99 latency > 500ms for 3m (large-model routes) OR > 200ms for small-model routes
  - Severity: P1
  - Notify: #platform-oncall and Owner
- Alert: GPU_POOL_EXHAUSTION
  - Condition: available GPUs in pool < 10% for 10m AND queue length increasing
  - Severity: P0 (if blocking Dedicated customers)
  - Notify: page primary and senior on-call

Alert tuning guidance
- Start with conservative thresholds and iterate after 1 week of real traffic.
- Use cardinality controls: avoid high-cardinality labels (user_id, request_id) in alert rules.
- When triaging flapping alerts, record root cause and add a short-term mute with timeline.

Runbooks (short form)
1) P0 — GPU fleet outage (symptoms: high queue, allocation failures, customer errors)
- Owner: infra-sre + Serving Runtime.
- Immediate steps:
  1. Acknowledge PagerDuty incident and announce to #platform-oncall.
  2. Verify control plane: `kubectl get pods -n gpu-system` and `kubectl logs -l app=gpu-orchestrator -n gpu-system`.
  3. Check node health: `kubectl describe node <node>` and cloud console (GPU attach/detach errors).
  4. If nodes are unhealthy due to driver or CUDA mismatch, follow GPU node remediation playbook (see section below).
  5. If capacity constraint, escalate to capacity-planning and open immediate autoscale burst (runbook: `./scripts/autoscale-gpu-burst.sh --pool <pool>`).
  6. If Dedicated customer impact, enable fallback routing to lower-tier model variants per routing policy.
  7. Post-incident: collect logs, kernel traces, and open a Jira (label: incident/gpu-outage).

2) P1 — Inference API high p99 latency
- Owner: Serving Runtime.
- Immediate steps:
  1. Check recent deploys in the last 60 minutes. `kubectl rollout history deployment/inference-api -n inference`
  2. Check CPU/GPU utilization and queue depth on the inference pods.
  3. Inspect KV cache hit ratio; low hit ratio can cause repeated re-compute. Dashboard: "PLATFORM / inference-api / cache-hit"
  4. If OOMs observed, check pod events and consider increasing memory request or rolling back recent model load.
  5. If traffic spike, consider enabling autoscale or route to dedicated pool.

GPU node remediation (common commands)
- Reboot node: `gcloud compute instances reset <instance-id>` (or equivalent in AWS/Azure).
- Check driver status: `nvidia-smi` and `dmesg | grep -i nvidia`.
- If driver mismatch: cordon node `kubectl cordon <node>` then drain `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets` and run node-reimage playbook.

Incident retrospective (last 30 days summary)
- Incident: GPU scheduling regressions on 2026-02-04 (P0, 2.5 hrs outage for Dedicated customers).
- Root cause: race condition in gpu-orchestrator's reconciliation loop under high churn + a recent kernel update on cloud images.
- Impact: 3 Dedicated customers observed elevated latency and failed allocations.
- Actions taken:
  - Rollback to previous orchestrator release (done during incident).
  - Hotfix: add stronger leader-election lock in gpu-orchestrator (deployed 2026-02-10).
  - Longer-term: implement canary for node image updates and add kernel-driver compatibility test in CI (scheduled Q2).
- Retrospective owner: Marcus Liu.

Post-incident improvements (status)
- Canaries for node images: in progress (target complete: 2026-03-15).
- Improved alerting around driver errors: deployed 2026-02-16.
- Runbook additions for immediate autoscale burst: documented here (complete).

Platform roadmap (Q2 2026 priorities)
- Q2-2026 M1: Robust GPU node canary pipeline (complete/integration testing).
- Q2-2026 M2: Dashboard standardization and templating for all platform services (owner: Observability).
- Q2-2026 M3: Alert noise reduction project: tag-based silencing and smarter suppression windows.
- Q2-2026 M4: KV cache autosizing and eviction analytics (reduce cold-starts for inference).
- Q2-2026 M5: Support for multi-tenant burst pools for Dedicated customers.

Team wiki & onboarding essentials
- Team wiki canonical pages: "Platform team wiki" (link in related_pages), "Oncall handbook" and "Runbook authoring guide".
- New hire checklist (platform engineer):
  1. Complete infra onboarding and request PagerDuty access.
  2. Read this playbook and two recent postmortems.
  3. Pair with a platform engineer for a deploy and for on-call shadowing (2 week shadow).
  4. Complete the Grafana/Dashboard tutorial and add one minor dashboard update.

Operational best practices
- Use feature flags for risky rollouts and default to gradual canaries (5% -> 25% -> 100%).
- Keep runbooks short, prescriptive, and example-driven. Document CLI commands and exact dashboard links.
- Run regular game days (quarterly) to validate runbooks and escalations.

Appendices
- A: Useful commands
  - `kubectl get pods -n <ns> -o wide`
  - `kubectl logs -l app=<service> -n <ns> --since=15m`
  - `gcloud compute instances list --filter='status=TERMINATED'`
- B: Contact list
  - Platform Core lead: platform-lead@redwood.com
  - Oncall rota: https://pagerduty.com/rotations/platform
